section_summary: The section concludes a study of the foreign credit and trade needed to restore Japan’s economy, followed by tables projecting production, imports, exports, and credit requirements. Later records address sterling trade, bank credit secured by Japanese assets, and the liquidation of corporate securities. The final documents concern repatriated currencies, unpaid bank capital, and a proposed rehabilitation appropriation.

subfiles.title: Possibility of a Balanced Japanese Economy: conclusion and supplementary tables
subfiles.about: Concludes a reconstruction study and tabulates projected production, trade, living standards, and foreign credit.
subfiles.summary: The conclusion says foreign aid alone cannot make Japan self-supporting: labor stability, domestic economic reform, workable foreign trade, regional recovery, and public acceptance of a low living standard are also required. It asks for Allied assistance while emphasizing Japanese effort. Ten supplementary tables project supplies, consumption, coal and steel allocation, employment, annual imports and exports, and credit needs through fiscal 1949–1950.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice for War 85805
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.about: Designates a white telegram copy to replace a missing yellow action copy.
subfiles.summary: White copy replaces the unreturned action copy of telegram War 85805.

subfiles.title: War 85805: proposed sterling trade arrangement
subfiles.about: Relays United States proposals for sterling trade between Japan and the United Kingdom’s sterling area.
subfiles.summary: The proposal places most Japanese trade with participating sterling-area countries on a sterling basis, excluding cotton textiles made from United States supplied cotton. It provides for a Bank of England account, dollar conversion rules, semiannual conversion dates, and settlement of existing balances. Australia’s adherence is considered essential; India and New Zealand are desirable participants.

subfiles.title: Arrangements for Securing Bank Credits to Finance Japanese Imports
subfiles.to: Mr. Havlik, OFD; Mr. Saltzman, SA
subfiles.about: Reviews proposed bank financing for Japanese imports secured by an import-export revolving fund.
subfiles.summary: Whitman describes a proposed $60 million raw-cotton credit, Export-Import Bank participation, and broader credit from private banks, backed by Japanese-owned convertible assets. He examines SCAP’s authority to pledge those assets, creditor priority, and bankers’ concerns about collateral remaining in Japan. He recommends faster bank consideration and a decision on moving some assets to the United States.

subfiles.title: Transmission of proposed policy statement on Japanese public finance
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Forwards SWNCC 362 with limits on seeking a Far Eastern Commission decision.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SWNCC 362, reserving formal submission unless needed to avert another policy.

subfiles.title: SWNCC memorandum forwarding proposed Japanese public finance policy
subfiles.about: Requests restricted transmission of approved SWNCC 362 to the United States FEC representative.
subfiles.summary: Requests transmission of SWNCC 362 without routine submission for an FEC policy decision.

subfiles.title: Swiss Legation memorandum on Japanese securities
subfiles.about: Submits additional bank and bondholder declarations concerning Japanese securities owned by Swiss citizens.
subfiles.summary: Requests forwarding two additional declarations through designated channels.

subfiles.title: Jacques Ruch statement of residence
subfiles.about: States his and his wife’s residences in connection with Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Ruch lists family residences in France, Switzerland, and New York.

subfiles.title: National City Bank letter on Jacques Ruch’s bonds
subfiles.from: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Confirms custody and licensing history of Great Consolidated Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: Confirms safekeeping of $3,000 in bonds and records supporting Ruch’s ownership.

subfiles.title: SCAP telegram on Japanese external assets
subfiles.about: Recommends government-level exchange of data on Japanese external assets.
subfiles.summary: SCAP warns that Japanese data contain substantial gaps and that a February 1948 report would lack authority if based on current information. It proposes exchanging asset data with governments where major Japanese holdings were located.

subfiles.title: Transmission of SWNCC 362 to American Mission, Nanking
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Nanking
subfiles.about: Sends the Japanese public finance policy statement, highlighting reparations compensation.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SWNCC 362 and directs attention to its reparations-compensation paragraph.

subfiles.title: Recent Developments in Program for Securing Bank Credits to Finance Japanese Imports
subfiles.to: Mr. Ness, OFD; Mr. Saltzman, A-S
subfiles.about: Updates the September bank-credit memorandum with SCAP’s and lenders’ positions.
subfiles.summary: SCAP opposed moving Japanese gold because of political repercussions but accepted possible sale of silver. Whitman reports continued Export-Import Bank legal concerns, a new United States policy giving trade deficits priority against certain assets, and unresolved private-bank questions about collateral safeguards. His earlier recommendations stand.

subfiles.title: Liquidation Program
subfiles.about: Compares estimates of securities subject to liquidation under occupation reforms.
subfiles.summary: The writer distinguishes mandatory liquidation already set in motion from uncertain effects of antimonopoly and deconcentration laws. Estimates of stocks and bonds may overlap, and the possible reach of the proposed deconcentration law remains unclear.

subfiles.title: Liquidation of Securities in Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a study and raises concern about the scale of planned securities liquidation.
subfiles.summary: Reinstein asks whether the extensive liquidation program can be carried out.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Information Note 107
subfiles.about: Forwards the requested note on liquidation of securities in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Information Note 107 on Japanese securities liquidation.

subfiles.title: Information on the Liquidation of Securities in Japan
subfiles.doc_type: information note with chronology and charts
subfiles.about: Estimates securities to be sold and traces the occupation’s corporate liquidation program.
subfiles.summary: The note estimates nearly 20 billion yen in paid-up share value for disposal through several agencies, while warning about double counting, inflation, and uncertain market values. It reviews obstacles to large-scale sales and the limited evidence of buyer interest. Its chronology and charts identify the laws, SCAP directives, agencies, and approximate holdings involved.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing drafts on Japanese credits
subfiles.about: Encloses draft Far Eastern Commission report and amendments to SCAP Circular No. 9.
subfiles.summary: Sends financing drafts for review before planned transmission to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Despatch 1398: repatriates’ currencies and financial instruments
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1812 on central custody of financial assets surrendered by repatriates.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a directive concentrating surrendered assets in the Bank of Japan.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1812: Concentration of Currencies and Financial Instruments Surrendered by Repatriates
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Orders central deposit, custody, and reporting of repatriates’ surrendered financial assets.
subfiles.summary: SCAP directs weekly deposit of covered currencies and instruments with the Bank of Japan, special custody pending disposition, an initial accounting by December 31, 1947, and monthly reports. Several Japanese and former occupation currencies are excepted.

subfiles.title: Despatch 1406: Interim Agreement for the Sterling Financing of Private Trade with Japan
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports the interim sterling agreement and transmits its text and press release.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes participants, sterling accounts, six-month conversion, and the cotton-textile exclusion.

subfiles.title: Interim Agreement for the Sterling Financing of Private Trade with Japan
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers and United Kingdom
subfiles.about: Sets temporary rules for accepting, spending, and converting sterling from private trade.
subfiles.summary: Provides for sterling trade accounts and dollar conversion after six months.

subfiles.title: Far East Command press release of November 15, 1947
subfiles.from: Far East Command, Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Announces the sterling arrangement alongside other occupation news.
subfiles.summary: The lead item announces the interim sterling trade arrangement and its participants. Other items cover radiotelegraph service, military entertainment and sports, Red Cross honors, Colonel Glasgow’s death, and holiday postal preparations.

subfiles.title: Despatch 8: further terms of the sterling trade agreement
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits clarification of dollar-sterling conversion rates and timing.
subfiles.summary: Reports use of IMF-registered rates and possible conversion after six months.

subfiles.title: SCAP memorandum clarifying sterling financing of private trade
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: Clarifies exchange rates and conversion rights under the interim sterling agreement.
subfiles.summary: Specifies IMF-registered rates for sales and later sterling-dollar conversion.

subfiles.title: Department of State charge slip
subfiles.about: Records an enclosure’s internal charge and routing.
subfiles.summary: Internal charge slip with sparse handwritten routing entries.

subfiles.title: Despatch 56: call for payment of financial institution capital stock
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1848 requiring payment of unpaid financial institution capital stock.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the ninety-day payment call and exceptions for specified holders.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1848: Call for Payment of Unpaid Capital Stock
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Orders a ninety-day call for unpaid capital stock of Japanese financial institutions.
subfiles.summary: Directs full payment, specifies consequences of default, and exempts closed institutions and certain foreign holders.

subfiles.title: Despatch 82: Economic Rehabilitation Occupied Areas estimate for Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Comments on the proposed fiscal 1948–1949 rehabilitation estimate for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Mission reviews a $452.3 million estimate, including $180.1 million sought from Congress, and questions assumptions that industrial rehabilitation will restore trade balance by 1953. The despatch continues beyond this section.
